content.value_statement: Writing mathematical notation in Obsidian can be slow and error-prone. This skill provides ready MathJax patterns for equations, symbols, matrices, and aligned formulas.
actual_capabilities: Formats inline and block MathJax expressions for Obsidian notes.
Provides syntax for fractions, roots, superscripts, subscripts, and binomial coefficients.
Maps common Greek letters, operators, set symbols, and logic symbols to LaTeX commands.
Shows matrix, aligned equation, cases, delimiter, and text-in-math patterns.
Supplies examples for integrals, sums, limits, derivatives, norms, and probability notation.
Includes a reference file with extended symbols, functions, environments, spacing, and accents.
limitations: It is a documentation skill, not a live MathJax renderer or preview engine.
It does not verify every formula for mathematical correctness.
It targets Obsidian MathJax behavior and may not match every LaTeX engine.
It does not install Obsidian plugins or modify vault settings.

use_cases.title: Prepare Lecture Notes
use_cases.description: Turn calculus, algebra, or probability formulas into Obsidian-ready MathJax blocks.

use_cases.title: Document Technical Research
use_cases.description: Use consistent notation for matrices, operators, symbol tables, and aligned derivations.

use_cases.title: Maintain Math Reference Notes
use_cases.description: Create quick symbol references and reusable formula patterns inside an Obsidian vault.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Equation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple formula.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this formula into Obsidian MathJax: [describe the equation]. Include inline and block versions.

prompt_templates.title: Format a Matrix
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for linear algebra notation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian MathJax matrix for [matrix values]. Use the best bracket style and explain the choice briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Aligned Derivation
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a multi-line aligned MathJax derivation for [problem]. Use clear alignment points and readable spacing.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Notation Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a compact Obsidian MathJax reference for [topic]. Include symbols, operators, common formulas, and usage notes.

output_examples.input: I need Bayes theorem for an Obsidian probability note.
output_examples.output: A ready-to-paste display equation for Bayes theorem, using conditional probability notation and clear fraction structure.

output_examples.input: I need a 3 by 3 identity matrix in square brackets.
output_examples.output: A block MathJax matrix using the bracketed matrix environment, with rows and columns aligned for Obsidian.

output_examples.input: I need a short reference for Greek letters and set symbols.
output_examples.output: A concise Obsidian note section listing common Greek letters, relation symbols, and set operators with their MathJax syntax.

best_practices: Use block equations for multi-line formulas, matrices, and derivations.
Use braces around multi-character superscripts and subscripts.
Use alignment environments when showing step-by-step transformations.
anti_patterns: Do not use display equations for every short inline symbol.
Do not omit braces when exponents or subscripts contain more than one character.
Do not assume all LaTeX packages are available in Obsidian MathJax.

faq.question: Does this skill render MathJax visually?
faq.answer: No. It provides Obsidian-ready MathJax syntax and examples, but Obsidian performs the visual rendering.

faq.question: Can it help with matrices?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common matrix environments, delimiters, determinants, identity matrices, and ellipsis patterns.

faq.question: Does it include symbol references?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference file includes Greek letters, operators, arrows, delimiters, fonts, spacing, accents, and environments.

faq.question: Is it specific to Obsidian?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples are written for MathJax syntax commonly used inside Obsidian notes.

faq.question: Can it check mathematical correctness?
faq.answer: No. It helps format notation, but users should verify the math and assumptions themselves.

faq.question: Does it require external commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation only and does not instruct the agent to run shell commands or scripts.
